claims.text: The massive Louvre Palace was actually first built as a defensive medieval fortress in the late 12th to 13th century under King Philip II.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Fascinatingly, you can still see the stone remnants of this original medieval fortress down in the basement of the museum today.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: In 1546, King Francis I completely transformed the old fortress, converting it into the primary grand residence of the French kings.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The palace's role changed forever in 1682 when King Louis XIV moved his royal household to the Palace of Versailles, leaving the Louvre to simply display the royal art collection.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: During the French Revolution, the National Assembly officially decreed that the building should become a public museum to display the nation's masterpieces.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The Louvre Museum officially opened its doors on 10 August 1793, featuring an initial exhibition of 537 paintings that were mostly confiscated church and royal property.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Today, it is a world-famous national art museum and the permanent home to iconic Western masterpieces like the Mona Lisa and the Venus de Milo.
claims.subject: self
